tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

"""
moonep build script. Compiles the CUDA extension `moonep._C` (the pybind11
module living in csrc/bindings.cu) into the `moonep` package so it can be
imported as `from moonep import _C` after either:

  pip install -e .                              # editable install (preferred)

or, for a quick in-place build without installing:

  python setup.py build_ext --inplace

The .so lands at `moonep/_C.<abi-tag>.so`.
"""

import os

from setuptools import find_packages, setup
from torch.utils.cpp_extension import BuildExtension, CUDAExtension


REPO_ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(__file__))


nvcc_flags = [
    "-O3",
    "--use_fast_math",
    "-std=c++20",
    "--expt-extended-lambda",
    "--expt-relaxed-constexpr",
    "-forward-unknown-to-host-compiler",
    "-Xcompiler=-Wno-psabi",
    "-Xcompiler=-fno-strict-aliasing",
    "-DNDEBUG",
    "-lineinfo",
    "-diag-suppress=3189",
    "-ftemplate-backtrace-limit=0",
    "-D__CUDA_NO_HALF_OPERATORS__",
    "-D__CUDA_NO_HALF_CONVERSIONS__",
    "-D__CUDA_NO_BFLOAT16_CONVERSIONS__",
    "-D__CUDA_NO_HALF2_OPERATORS__",
]

cxx_flags = [
    "-O3",
    "-fno-strict-aliasing",
    "-Wno-psabi",
]


ext_modules = [
    CUDAExtension(
        name="moonep._C",
        sources=[
            os.path.join("csrc", "bindings.cu"),
        ],
        include_dirs=[
            os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "csrc"),
        ],
        libraries=["cuda"],
        extra_compile_args={
            "cxx": cxx_flags,
            "nvcc": nvcc_flags,
        },
    ),
]


setup(
    name="moonep",
    version="0.0.1",
    packages=find_packages(include=["moonep", "moonep.*"]),
    install_requires=[
        "nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.4.2",
    ],
    ext_modules=ext_modules,
    cmdclass={"build_ext": BuildExtension},
)

1	"""
2	MoonEP Top-level API.
3	
4	Notation: S = input tokens per rank, K = routed top-k per token, E = total routed
5	experts in the EP group, R = number of EP ranks (EP comm size), B = weight
6	prefetch slots per rank, NvS = dispatched token slots per rank (S*K real
7	tokens plus per-VM-group padding), H = hidden size, H' = expert FFN
8	intermediate size.
9	
10	Usage:
11	    buffer = Buffer(S, H, K, E, num_ep_ranks, num_sms=None, token_padding=128)
12	
13	    # dispatch fwd
14	    hidden_nvsh, route_weights_nvs, cu_seqlens, plan = buffer.dispatch(
15	        hidden_sh, route_weights_sk, topk_experts_sk, tokens_per_expert,
16	    )
17	    buffer.prefetch_weight(
18	        plan=plan,
19	        full_gate_weight=full_gate_weight,
20	        full_up_weight=full_up_weight,
21	        full_down_weight=full_down_weight,
22	    )
23	
24	    # combine fwd
25	    output_sh, gathered_route_weights_sk, _ = buffer.combine(
26	        plan=plan,
27	        hidden_nvsh=expert_output_nvsh,
28	        route_weights_nvs=route_weights_nvs,
29	    )
30	
31	    # combine bwd: re-dispatch the output grad with the saved plan
32	    grad_expert_output_nvsh, _, _, _ = buffer.dispatch(grad_output_sh, plan=plan)
33	
34	    # dispatch bwd: combine the hidden grad back to token-major, and reduce
35	    # duplicated experts' weight grads to their home ranks
36	    grad_hidden_sh, _, _ = buffer.combine(plan=plan, hidden_nvsh=grad_hidden_nvsh)
37	    buffer.reduce_grad(
38	        plan=plan,
39	        full_gate_grad=full_gate_grad,
40	        full_up_grad=full_up_grad,
41	        full_down_grad=full_down_grad,
42	        gate_reduce_buffer=gate_reduce_buffer,
43	        up_reduce_buffer=up_reduce_buffer,
44	        down_reduce_buffer=down_reduce_buffer,
45	    )
46	
47	    buffer.destroy()
48	"""
49	
50	import logging
51	import os
52	import warnings
53	
54	import torch
55	import torch.distributed as dist
56	
57	from .buffer import (
58	    create_nvl_dist_tensor,
59	    create_nvl_dist_multicast_tensor,
60	    pad_dim0_for_alignment,
61	    get_vmm_granularity,
62	    get_multicast_granularity,
63	)
64	from .constants import DEDUP_BUILDER_WARPS
65	from .planning import MoonEPCommPlan, allocate_planning_outputs, launch_planning
66	from .inter_rank_sync import launch_inter_rank_sync
67	from .dispatch import launch_dispatch
68	from .dispatch_epilogue import launch_dispatch_epilogue
69	from .combine import launch_combine
70	from .combine_prologue import launch_combine_prologue
71	from .prefetch import _ELEM_TYPES, launch_prefetch, retile_for_prefetch
72	from .grad_reduce import launch_grad_reduce
73	
74	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
75	
76	
77	def _align_up(x: int, alignment: int) -> int:
78	    """Round x up to a multiple of alignment."""
79	    return ((x + alignment - 1) // alignment) * alignment
80	
81	
82	def _num_sms_dedup_from_env(max_sms: int) -> int:
83	    """Resolve the local epilogue/prologue SM count.
84	
85	    ``MOONEP_NUM_SMS_DEDUP`` is intentionally an environment override rather
86	    than a Buffer argument so benchmark jobs can sweep it without touching the
87	    public API surface.
88	    """
89	    raw = os.environ.get("MOONEP_NUM_SMS_DEDUP")
90	    if raw is None or raw == "":
91	        return max_sms
92	    try:
93	        value = int(raw)
94	    except ValueError as exc:
95	        raise ValueError(
96	            f"MOONEP_NUM_SMS_DEDUP must be an integer in [1, {max_sms}], got {raw!r}"
97	        ) from exc
98	    if not (1 <= value <= max_sms):
99	        raise ValueError(
100	            f"MOONEP_NUM_SMS_DEDUP must be in [1, {max_sms}], got {value}"
101	        )
102	    return value
103

105	def _log_context_buffer_size(ctx: dict) -> None:
106	    def tensor_nbytes(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> int:
107	        return int(tensor.numel()) * int(tensor.element_size())
108	
109	    def format_nbytes(nbytes: int) -> str:
110	        if nbytes >= 1 << 30:
111	            return f"{nbytes / (1 << 30):.2f} GiB"
112	        if nbytes >= 1 << 20:
113	            return f"{nbytes / (1 << 20):.2f} MiB"
114	        if nbytes >= 1 << 10:
115	            return f"{nbytes / (1 << 10):.2f} KiB"
116	        return f"{nbytes} B"
117	
118	    if int(ctx['rank']) != 0:
119	        return
120	
121	    R = int(ctx['R'])
122	    hidden_mapped_bytes = tensor_nbytes(ctx['hidden_buf'])
123	    meta_mapped_bytes = tensor_nbytes(ctx['meta_buf'])
124	    hidden_chunk_bytes = hidden_mapped_bytes // R
125	    meta_chunk_bytes = meta_mapped_bytes // R
126	    local_temp_bytes = sum(
127	        tensor_nbytes(ctx[name])
128	        for name in (
129	            'alloc',
130	            'group_tokens',
131	            'z',
132	            'local_hist',
133	            'grid_sync_bar',
134	            'primary_packed',
135	            'kmask',
136	            'kidx_to_loff',
137	            'builder_bar',
138	        )
139	    )
140	
141	    total_buffer_bytes = hidden_chunk_bytes + meta_chunk_bytes + local_temp_bytes
142	
143	    log_lines = [
144	        "MoonEP comm buffer sizes:",
145	        "  config                 : "
146	        f"R={ctx['R']}, S={ctx['S']}, H={ctx['H']}, E={ctx['E']}, "
147	        f"K={ctx['K']}, NvS={ctx['NvS']}, NvS_padded={ctx['NvS_padded']}",
148	        "  sm_count               : "
149	        f"num_sms={ctx['num_sms']}, num_sms_dedup={ctx['num_sms_dedup']}",
150	        f"  hidden_buffer_size     : {format_nbytes(hidden_chunk_bytes)}",
151	        f"  meta_buffer_size       : {format_nbytes(meta_chunk_bytes)}",
152	        f"  local_temp_buffer_size : {format_nbytes(local_temp_bytes)}",
153	        f"  total_size             : {format_nbytes(total_buffer_bytes)}",
154	    ]
155	    logger.info("\n".join(log_lines))

222	def _create_context(
223	    S: int,
224	    H: int,
225	    K: int,
226	    E: int,
227	    num_ep_ranks: int,
228	    num_sms: int | None = None,
229	    token_padding: int = 128,
230	    B: int | None = None,
231	    group: "dist.ProcessGroup | None" = None,
232	) -> dict:
233	    """Pre-allocate all NVLink shared buffers and local temp buffers.
234	
235	    The extra logical NvS slots from token_padding are allocated as
236	    (token_padding - 1) * 2 * E / num_ep_ranks; the physical allocation is
237	    still aligned to VMM granularity.
238	    NVLink shared buffer layout:
239	      - hidden_buf: [NvS_padded, H] bf16 — separate allocation, padded for VMM alignment
240	      - meta_buf:   [meta_chunk_padded] int32 — merged allocation containing:
241	          [0, NvS):                weights (fp32, alias as int32)
242	          [NvS, NvS + R*E):       tpe gather (only rank 0 is the read/write target; symmetric reserve)
243	          [NvS + R*E, ...):       planning internal scratch/staging
244	          [..., +N4):             topk0 offload scratch
245	          [..., +N4):             ORDER, c1 order consumed by c2/passB
246	          [..., +N4):             ORDER0, rank1 rank0-c1 scratch
247	          [..., +3):              cross-rank phase barrier
248	          [..., +NvS):            src_info scratch published by planning and
249	                                  consumed by the fresh dispatch dedup builder;
250	                                  non-negative entries encode src_rank * NvS + offv,
251	                                  -1 marks empty slots
252	    """
253	    if num_sms is None:
254	        num_sms = 32
255	    assert isinstance(num_sms, int) and num_sms > 0, \
256	        f"num_sms must be a positive int, got {num_sms}"
257	    rank = dist.get_rank(group=group)
258	    R = num_ep_ranks
259	    assert R == dist.get_world_size(group=group), (
260	        f"num_ep_ranks ({R}) must equal group world size "
261	        f"({dist.get_world_size(group=group)})"
262	    )
263	    N = S * K
264	    device = torch.cuda.current_device()
265	    dev = f"cuda:{device}"
266	    max_sms = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device).multi_processor_count
267	    num_sms_dedup = _num_sms_dedup_from_env(max_sms)
268	
269	    epn = E // R
270	    assert E % R == 0, f"E ({E}) must be divisible by R ({R})"
271	    assert isinstance(token_padding, int) and token_padding > 0, \
272	        f"token_padding must be a positive int, got {token_padding}"
273	    if B is None:
274	        B = epn
275	    assert isinstance(B, int) and B > 0, f"B must be a positive int, got {B}"
276	
277	    NvS_capacity = S * K
278	
279	    # The current constructive planner lets each destination rank receive
280	    # tokens from at most one remote home group. Each home group has E/R
281	    # experts, so each rank has at most E/R remote expert segments, plus at
282	    # most E/R local expert segments. Each non-empty segment is padded up
283	    # from at least 1 real token slot to a multiple of token_padding, so the
284	    # extra logical NvS slot bound is (token_padding - 1) * 2 * E/R. The
285	    # physical allocation below is still aligned to VMM granularity via
286	    # pad_dim0_for_alignment() / pad_to_granularity().
287	    token_padding_extra = (token_padding - 1) * 2 * epn
288	    NvS = NvS_capacity + token_padding_extra
289	
290	    # ================================================================
291	    # Planning constexpr computation and int32 range guards
292	    # ================================================================
293	    BLOCK_SIZE_P2 = 2048
294	
295	    int32_max = 2**31 - 1
296	    assert 0 < N < int32_max, (
297	        "planning requires 0 < S*K < int32_max: "
298	        f"S={S}, K={K}, S*K={N}, int32_max={int32_max}"
299	    )
300	    num_vblocks = (N + BLOCK_SIZE_P2 - 1) // BLOCK_SIZE_P2
301	
302	    # ================================================================
303	    # Compute padded dimensions for VMM alignment
304	    # ================================================================
305	    NvS_padded = pad_dim0_for_alignment([NvS, H], torch.bfloat16)
306	
307	    # Meta offsets are int32 elements. Vectorized regions are 16B-aligned.
308	    WEIGHTS_OFF = 0
309	    TPE_OFF = _align_up(NvS, 4)
310	    PLAN_OFF = _align_up(TPE_OFF + R * E, 4)
311	    broadcast_elems = 3 * E * R
312	    assert broadcast_elems % 4 == 0, (
313	        f"broadcast_elems ({broadcast_elems}) must be divisible by 4"
314	    )
315	    planning_out_elems = (
316	        broadcast_elems
317	        + R * (E + B)
318	        + 2 * R * (E + B)
319	        + B * R
320	        + 2 * R
321	    )
322	
323	    # C1 scratch segments are padded so bulk copies can stay vectorized.
324	    N4 = _align_up(N, 4)
325	    TOPK0_OFF = _align_up(PLAN_OFF + planning_out_elems, 4)
326	    ORDER_OFF = TOPK0_OFF + N4
327	    ORDER0_OFF = ORDER_OFF + N4
328	    BARRIER_OFF = ORDER0_OFF + N4
329	    # cross_rank_barrier uses 3 int32 per rank: 2 phase signals + 1 phase/sign
330	    # counter (independent of rank count, self-resetting double buffer).
331	    BARRIER_SLOTS = 3
332	    SRC_INFO_OFF = BARRIER_OFF + BARRIER_SLOTS
333	    meta_chunk_logical = SRC_INFO_OFF + NvS
334	
335	    # Chunk size must satisfy both VMM mapping and multicast binding.
336	    gran = get_vmm_granularity()
337	    mc_gran = get_multicast_granularity(R)
338	    chunk_align_bytes = max(gran, mc_gran)
339	    meta_chunk_bytes = meta_chunk_logical * 4
340	    meta_chunk_padded = _align_up(meta_chunk_bytes, chunk_align_bytes) // 4
341	
342	    # Some CuTe DSL address expressions multiply a runtime Int32 rank/drank by
343	    # these constexpr strides, so guard the largest reachable nonnegative index.
344	    max_meta_index = (R - 1) * meta_chunk_padded + meta_chunk_logical - 1
345	    assert max_meta_index <= int32_max, (
346	        "meta_buf rank-stride indexing would overflow CuTe Int32 arithmetic: "
347	        f"max_index={max_meta_index}, R={R}, S={S}, K={K}, N={N}, "
348	        f"NvS={NvS}, meta_chunk_logical={meta_chunk_logical}, "
349	        f"meta_chunk_padded={meta_chunk_padded}, int32_max={int32_max}"
350	    )
351	    max_hidden_index = (R - 1) * NvS_padded + NvS - 1
352	    assert max_hidden_index <= int32_max, (
353	        "hidden_buf/dst rank-stride indexing would overflow CuTe Int32 arithmetic: "
354	        f"max_index={max_hidden_index}, R={R}, S={S}, K={K}, N={N}, "
355	        f"NvS={NvS}, NvS_padded={NvS_padded}, int32_max={int32_max}"
356	    )
357	
358	    # ================================================================
359	    # Allocate NVLink shared buffers
360	    # ================================================================
361	    hidden_buf = create_nvl_dist_tensor([NvS_padded, H], torch.bfloat16, rank, R, group=group)
362	    meta_buf, meta_mc = create_nvl_dist_multicast_tensor(
363	        [meta_chunk_padded], torch.int32, rank, R, group=group,
364	    )
365	
366	    # Zero the barrier region on all ranks
367	    for r in range(R):
368	        meta_buf[r * meta_chunk_padded + BARRIER_OFF:
369	                 r * meta_chunk_padded + BARRIER_OFF + BARRIER_SLOTS].zero_()
370	    dist.barrier(group=group)
371	
372	
373	    # ================================================================
374	    # Local buffers
375	    # ================================================================
376	    alloc = torch.empty(E * R, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
377	    group_tokens = torch.empty(R, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
378	    z = torch.empty(R * R, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
379	    local_hist = torch.empty(E * num_vblocks, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
380	    # Global arrive counter (1 int32) for the software grid barrier: the
381	    # equivalent of cudaLaunchCooperative's grid workspace. Self-resetting
382	    # (sentinel-bit flip), allocated once and shared by planning/dispatch/
383	    # combine/inter_rank, with no per-launch zeroing needed.
384	    grid_sync_bar = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
385	    # Dispatch builder scratch for fresh planning. ``kidx_to_loff`` maps each
386	    # (source rank, token, topk index) key to the local NvS slot used later when
387	    # expanding duplicate groups. ``builder_bar`` is a self-resetting TAG
388	    # counter, so it is initialized once like grid_sync_bar.
389	    primary_packed = torch.empty(R * S, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
390	    kmask = torch.empty(R * S, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
391	    kidx_to_loff = torch.empty(R * S * K, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
392	    builder_bar = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
393	
394	    ctx = {
395	        'rank': rank,
396	        'group': group,
397	        'R': R, 'E': E, 'S': S, 'K': K, 'H': H,
398	        'B': B,
399	        'N': N, 'NvS': NvS,
400	        'NvS_capacity': NvS_capacity,
401	        'NvS_padded': NvS_padded,
402	        'num_sms': num_sms,
403	        'num_sms_dedup': num_sms_dedup,
404	        'token_padding': token_padding,
405	        'device': device,
406	        'token_padding_extra': token_padding_extra,
407	        # NVLink shared
408	        'hidden_buf': hidden_buf,
409	        'meta_buf': meta_buf,
410	        'meta_mc': meta_mc,
411	        # Meta layout
412	        'meta_chunk_padded': meta_chunk_padded,
413	        'WEIGHTS_OFF': WEIGHTS_OFF,
414	        'TPE_OFF': TPE_OFF,
415	        'PLAN_OFF': PLAN_OFF,
416	        'TOPK0_OFF': TOPK0_OFF,
417	        'ORDER_OFF': ORDER_OFF,
418	        'ORDER0_OFF': ORDER0_OFF,
419	        'BARRIER_OFF': BARRIER_OFF,
420	        'SRC_INFO_OFF': SRC_INFO_OFF,
421	        # Local temps
422	        'alloc': alloc, 'group_tokens': group_tokens,
423	        'z': z,
424	        'local_hist': local_hist,
425	        'grid_sync_bar': grid_sync_bar,
426	        'primary_packed': primary_packed,
427	        'kmask': kmask,
428	        'kidx_to_loff': kidx_to_loff,
429	        'builder_bar': builder_bar,
430	        'num_vblocks': num_vblocks,
431	        # Local views
432	        'hidden_buf_local': hidden_buf[rank * NvS_padded: rank * NvS_padded + NvS],
433	        'weights_buf_local': meta_buf[rank * meta_chunk_padded + WEIGHTS_OFF:
434	                                      rank * meta_chunk_padded + WEIGHTS_OFF + NvS],
435	    }
436	    _log_context_buffer_size(ctx)
437	    return ctx

440	class Buffer:
441	    """MoonEP communication buffer owner.
442	
443	    A Buffer owns the NVLink/VMM communication buffers, local scratch tensors,
444	    and the async communication stream used by dispatch/prefetch/combine/reduce. Call
445	    ``destroy()`` before tearing down the process group.
446	    """
447	
448	    def __init__(
449	        self,
450	        S: int,
451	        H: int,
452	        K: int,
453	        E: int,
454	        num_ep_ranks: int,
455	        num_sms: int | None = None,
456	        token_padding: int = 128,
457	        B: int | None = None,
458	        group: "dist.ProcessGroup | None" = None,
459	        comm_stream_priority: int = -1,
460	        enable_pdl: bool = True,
461	        explicitly_destroy: bool = False,
462	    ):
463	        """Allocate and hold all communication buffers.
464	
465	        Args:
466	            S: input tokens per rank.
467	            H: hidden size.
468	            K: routed top-k per token.
469	            E: total routed experts in the EP group; must be divisible by
470	                ``num_ep_ranks``.
471	            num_ep_ranks: EP group size (R); must equal the group world size.
472	            num_sms: SM count for the comm kernels; None defaults to 32.
473	            token_padding: each non-empty VM group is padded up to a multiple
474	                of this token count.
475	            B: weight prefetch slots per rank; None defaults to
476	                ``E // num_ep_ranks``.
477	            group: torch.distributed process group; None uses the default
478	                group. Must be called after ``init_process_group``.
479	            comm_stream_priority: priority of the async comm stream; the
480	                default -1 gives it higher priority than the main stream.
481	            enable_pdl: launch kernels with programmatic dependent launch;
482	                False falls back to plain same-stream serial launches.
483	            explicitly_destroy: if True, warn (instead of auto-destroying)
484	                when the Buffer is garbage-collected without ``destroy()``.
485	        """
486	        assert isinstance(comm_stream_priority, int), (
487	            f"comm_stream_priority must be an int, got "
488	            f"{type(comm_stream_priority).__name__}"
489	        )
490	        assert isinstance(enable_pdl, bool), (
491	            f"enable_pdl must be a bool, got {type(enable_pdl).__name__}"
492	        )
493	        self.explicitly_destroy = explicitly_destroy
494	        self.comm_stream_priority = comm_stream_priority
495	        self.enable_pdl = enable_pdl
496	        self._comm_stream: torch.cuda.Stream | None = None
497	        self._destroyed = False
498	        self._ctx = _create_context(
499	            S, H, K, E, num_ep_ranks,
500	            num_sms=num_sms,
501	            token_padding=token_padding,
502	            B=B,
503	            group=group,
504	        )
505	        self._comm_stream = torch.cuda.Stream(
506	            device=int(self._ctx['device']),
507	            priority=self.comm_stream_priority,
508	        )
509	
510	    @property
511	    def destroyed(self) -> bool:
512	        return self._destroyed
513	
514	    @property
515	    def hidden_nvsh_buffer_view(self) -> torch.Tensor:
516	        """The local rank's [NvS, H] bf16 communication buffer.
517	
518	        Exposed for zero-copy integration: callers may write expert outputs
519	        into this view and hand it back to ``combine(zero_copy=True)``. The
520	        view aliases persistent comm state that every dispatch/combine on
521	        this Buffer overwrites — never let it (or any tensor sharing its
522	        storage) cross into autograd-saved state.
523	        """
524	        return self._require_ctx()['hidden_buf_local']
525	
526	    @property
527	    def router_weight_buffer_view(self) -> torch.Tensor:
528	        """fp32 view of the local rank's [NvS] route-weights comm buffer.
529	
530	        Same aliasing/lifetime rules as ``hidden_nvsh_buffer_view``.
531	        """
532	        return self._require_ctx()['weights_buf_local'].view(torch.float32)
533	
534	    def _require_ctx(self) -> dict:
535	        assert not self._destroyed, "MoonEP Buffer has been destroyed"
536	        assert self._ctx is not None, "MoonEP Buffer is not initialized"
537	        return self._ctx
538	
539	    def destroy(self) -> None:
540	        """Synchronize and release all VMM/NVLink resources held by this Buffer.
541	
542	        Must be called before tearing down the process group. Idempotent.
543	        """
544	        if self._destroyed:
545	            return
546	        ctx = self._ctx
547	        if ctx is None:
548	            self._destroyed = True
549	            return
550	
551	        if self._comm_stream is not None:
552	            self._comm_stream.synchronize()
553	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
554	        group = ctx.get('group')
555	        if dist.is_initialized():
556	            dist.barrier(group=group)
557	
558	        # Drop views before owners. Tensor deleters release VMM mappings and
559	        # multicast handles once the Python references disappear.
560	        for key in (
561	            'hidden_buf_local',
562	            'weights_buf_local',
563	            'meta_mc',
564	            'meta_buf',
565	            'hidden_buf',
566	            'alloc',
567	            'group_tokens',
568	            'z',
569	            'local_hist',
570	            'grid_sync_bar',
571	            'primary_packed',
572	            'kmask',
573	            'kidx_to_loff',
574	            'builder_bar',
575	        ):
576	            ctx.pop(key, None)
577	        ctx.clear()
578	        self._ctx = None
579	        self._comm_stream = None
580	        self._destroyed = True
581	
582	    def __del__(self):
583	        if getattr(self, "_destroyed", True):
584	            return
585	        if getattr(self, "explicitly_destroy", False):
586	            warnings.warn(
587	                "MoonEP Buffer was not destroyed explicitly; resources may leak.",
588	                ResourceWarning,
589	            )
590	            return
591	        try:
592	            self.destroy()
593	        except Exception as exc:
594	            warnings.warn(
595	                f"MoonEP Buffer destructor failed to destroy resources: {exc!r}",
596	                ResourceWarning,
597	            )
598	
599	    @staticmethod
600	    def _record_streams(tensors, stream: torch.cuda.Stream) -> None:
601	        for t in tensors:
602	            if t is not None:
603	                t.record_stream(stream)
604	
605	    @staticmethod
606	    def _plan_runtime_tensors(plan: MoonEPCommPlan):
607	        return (
608	            plan.dst,
609	            plan.experts_to_copy,
610	            plan.zero_fill_ranges,
611	            plan.remote_stats,
612	            plan.dup_groups,
613	            plan.dup_loffs,
614	            plan.dup_counts,
615	        )
616	
617	    def _run_dispatch_on_current_stream(
618	        self,
619	        ctx: dict,
620	        hidden_sh: torch.Tensor,
621	        route_weights_sk: torch.Tensor | None,
622	        planning_args,
623	        plan: MoonEPCommPlan,
624	        hidden_nvsh: torch.Tensor,
625	        route_weights_nvs: torch.Tensor | None,
626	        *,
627	        inter_rank_sync: bool,
628	        zero_copy: bool,
629	        route_weights_zero_copy: bool,
630	    ) -> None:
631	        if inter_rank_sync:
632	            launch_inter_rank_sync(ctx)
633	
634	        if planning_args is not None:
635	            topk_flat, tokens_per_expert, cu_seqlens = planning_args
636	            launch_planning(ctx, topk_flat, tokens_per_expert, cu_seqlens, plan)
637	
638	        # Fresh planning publishes dst/src_info immediately before dispatch, so
639	        # dispatch can safely materialize the plan-owned dedup structures from
640	        # those temporaries. Plan-reuse paths must keep the saved structures
641	        # untouched. Dispatch also zero-fills the segment-padding rows of the
642	        # local shard (zero warp, plan.zero_fill_ranges).
643	        launch_dispatch(
644	            ctx,
645	            hidden_sh,
646	            route_weights_sk,
647	            plan,

725	        tokens_per_expert: torch.Tensor | None = None,
726	        plan: MoonEPCommPlan | None = None,
727	        async_finish: bool = False,
728	        *,
729	        inter_rank_sync: bool = True,
730	        zero_copy: bool = False,
731	        router_weights_zero_copy: bool = False,
732	    ):
733	        """dispatch fwd: run planning (unless reusing a plan) and scatter tokens
734	        to their expert-grouped positions on remote ranks.
735	
736	        Args:
737	            hidden_sh: [S, H] bf16 input tokens.
738	            route_weights_sk: [S, K] fp32 routing weights; None skips the
739	                weights buffer entirely.
740	            topk_experts_sk: [S, K] int32 expert ids; required when ``plan``
741	                is None.
742	            tokens_per_expert: [E] int32 local token count per expert;
743	                required when ``plan`` is None.
744	            plan: saved MoonEPCommPlan to reuse — planning is skipped and
745	                ``topk_experts_sk`` / ``tokens_per_expert`` are ignored. This
746	                is the combine bwd path: re-dispatching ``grad_output_sh``
747	                with the fwd plan scatters the output grad back to VM group
748	                order.
749	            async_finish: run on the comm stream and append a CUDA event to
750	                the return value.
751	            inter_rank_sync: run a CuTe DSL rank sync before planning
752	                (default True).
753	            zero_copy: return a view of the communication buffer
754	                (``hidden_buf_local``) instead of a fresh tensor. The view
755	                aliases state that the next dispatch/combine on this Buffer
756	                overwrites, so callers must not keep it across communication
757	                calls (in particular autograd must not save it for backward
758	                — that is exactly the case that requires ``zero_copy=False``).
759	                Row content is only defined within the ``cu_seqlens``-covered
760	                padded segments.
761	            router_weights_zero_copy: like ``zero_copy`` but for
762	                ``route_weights_nvs`` (the fp32 view of ``weights_buf_local``).

764	                view is the dangerous special case (tiny tensor, commonly
765	                saved into autograd state by training frameworks), so callers
766	                that only consume it before the next dispatch — e.g.
767	                inference — opt in explicitly.

769	        Returns:

771	            comm-stream CUDA event when ``async_finish=True``:

792	        else:
793	            cu_seqlens = None
794	            planning_args = None

796	
797	        if zero_copy:
798	            hidden_nvsh = ctx['hidden_buf_local']
799	        else:
800	            hidden_nvsh = torch.empty_like(ctx['hidden_buf_local'])
801	        if route_weights_sk is None:
802	            route_weights_nvs = None
803	        elif router_weights_zero_copy:
804	            route_weights_nvs = ctx['weights_buf_local'].view(torch.float32)
805	        else:
806	            route_weights_nvs = torch.empty(
807	                ctx['NvS'], dtype=torch.float32, device=ctx['meta_buf'].device
808	            )
809	
810	        if not async_finish:
811	            self._run_dispatch_on_current_stream(
812	                ctx,
813	                hidden_sh,
814	                route_weights_sk,
815	                planning_args,
816	                plan,
817	                hidden_nvsh,
818	                route_weights_nvs,
819	                inter_rank_sync=inter_rank_sync,
820	                zero_copy=zero_copy,
821	                route_weights_zero_copy=router_weights_zero_copy,
822	            )
823	            return hidden_nvsh, route_weights_nvs, cu_seqlens, plan
824	
825	        main_stream = torch.cuda.current_stream()
826	        comm = self._comm_stream
827	        assert comm is not None, "MoonEP Buffer communication stream is not initialized"
828	
829	        tensors_to_record = [
830	            hidden_sh,
831	            route_weights_sk,
832	            hidden_nvsh,
833	            route_weights_nvs,

835	        ]

839	
840	        input_ready = main_stream.record_event()

843	        with torch.cuda.stream(comm):

916	        else:
917	            scale_prefetch_args = None

"""
MoonEP Top-level API.

Notation: S = input tokens per rank, K = routed top-k per token, E = total routed
experts in the EP group, R = number of EP ranks (EP comm size), B = weight
prefetch slots per rank, NvS = dispatched token slots per rank (S*K real
tokens plus per-VM-group padding), H = hidden size, H' = expert FFN
intermediate size.

Usage:
    buffer = Buffer(S, H, K, E, num_ep_ranks, num_sms=None, token_padding=128)

    # dispatch fwd
    hidden_nvsh, route_weights_nvs, cu_seqlens, plan = buffer.dispatch(
        hidden_sh, route_weights_sk, topk_experts_sk, tokens_per_expert,
    )
    buffer.prefetch_weight(
        plan=plan,
        full_gate_weight=full_gate_weight,
        full_up_weight=full_up_weight,
        full_down_weight=full_down_weight,
    )

    # combine fwd
    output_sh, gathered_route_weights_sk, _ = buffer.combine(
        plan=plan,
        hidden_nvsh=expert_output_nvsh,
        route_weights_nvs=route_weights_nvs,
    )

    # combine bwd: re-dispatch the output grad with the saved plan
    grad_expert_output_nvsh, _, _, _ = buffer.dispatch(grad_output_sh, plan=plan)

    # dispatch bwd: combine the hidden grad back to token-major, and reduce
    # duplicated experts' weight grads to their home ranks
    grad_hidden_sh, _, _ = buffer.combine(plan=plan, hidden_nvsh=grad_hidden_nvsh)
    buffer.reduce_grad(
        plan=plan,
        full_gate_grad=full_gate_grad,
        full_up_grad=full_up_grad,
        full_down_grad=full_down_grad,
        gate_reduce_buffer=gate_reduce_buffer,
        up_reduce_buffer=up_reduce_buffer,
        down_reduce_buffer=down_reduce_buffer,
    )

    buffer.destroy()
"""

import logging
import os
import warnings

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
